name: M2a_test

args.name: submodel
args.description: Codon model as a function of omega

args.name: omega0
args.description: The omega value for conserved sites

args.name: p0
args.description: The fraction of conserved sites within the conserved/neutral mixture

args.name: posP
args.description: The fraction of sites in the positive-selection category

args.name: posW
args.description: The omega value for the positive-selection category under the alternative

args.name: posSelection
args.description: The model selector: 1 if positive selection, 0 if not

description:
This model performs a Bayesian version of the test of M2a against M1a. The posterior probability that posSelection=1 is the posterior probability of positive selection in the overall model comparison, not a probability for an individual site.

The conserved, neutral, and positive-selection categories have weights (1-posP)*p0, (1-posP)*(1-p0), and posP. The first two have omega values omega0 and 1. The positive-selection category has omega=posW under the alternative (posSelection=1) and omega=1 under the null (posSelection=0).

The default background uses GTR, MNM, and MutSelAA. Here omega scales nonsynonymous rates after accounting for amino-acid fitnesses. Thus omega=1 retains these fitness effects; neutrality and positive selection are assessed relative to this background.

Average PrPosSelection to estimate the posterior probability of positive selection; it can give a more accurate estimate than averaging posSelection. Use statreport to summarize LogOddsPosSelection; do not average that field directly.

citation.title: Accuracy and Power of Statistical Methods for Detecting Adaptive Evolution in Protein Coding Sequences and for Identifying Positively Selected Sites
